title: Chronological Access Narrative exporter for Residency-focused Audits
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Customers and auditors ask for compact, tamper-evident packages that explain who had access, how access changed, and where data residency/residency exceptions applied during an audit window. Current evidence exports are siloed (SCIM delta, SAML session logs, RBAC snapshots, manual review spreadsheets) and require significant manual stitching. This causes slow auditor response times and repeated follow-ups for residency context and retention justifications.

Goal:
Deliver an automated 'Chronological Access Narrative' exporter that stitches SCIM change events, RBAC policy deltas, SAML session correlations, and periodic access-review outcomes into a single chronological artifact. The artifact will include residency tags per tenant, retention metadata, and a signed manifest for tamper evidence suitable for auditor consumption.

Scope (MVP):
- Consume SCIM change stream (create/update/deactivate) and produce normalized access-events.
- Ingest RBAC policy change events (role edits, role assignments/removals) from internal event bus.
- Correlate SAML session logs to access-events to provide proof-of-use for privileged roles.
- Attach periodic access-review decisions (approve/revoke/escalation notes) to the timeline.
- Generate a residency-aware manifest: tenant residency (region), retention policy applied, and evidence retention expiry.
- Output format: compressed, signed ZIP with human-readable timeline (CSV or HTML), JSON index, and signature file.

Non-goals (MVP):
- Full interactive UI in Console (will provide links to download artifacts from S3).
- Real-time streaming delivery to external auditors (post-MVP).

Acceptance criteria:
1) For a given tenant and audit window, system produces a single ZIP containing: normalized-events.csv, index.json, review-notes.md, and manifest.sig.
2) Events are ordered by event_time and include source (SCIM|RBAC|SAML|REVIEW), actor, target, change_type, residency_tag, and retention_ttl.
3) Manifest includes SHA256 checksums for every file and is signed with the platform evidence key.
4) Export generation time <= 2 minutes for 30k events and storage size < 50MB compressed.
5) Unit and integration tests cover event normalization, residency tagging, and signature verification.

Proposed design (high level):
- Event ingestion: read from existing SCIM delta topic and RBAC-change topic. Normalize to canonical AccessEvent record in a lightweight streaming processor (Flink job or internal stream lambda).
- Correlation: join SAML session logs on principal ID and time window to attach session-proof-of-use fields.
- Residency enrichment: query tenant metadata store for residency region and attach residency_tag and applicable retention_policy.
- Export builder: on request (UI/API) or scheduled run for tenants in audit-mode, materialize ordered events into files, compute hashes, and sign manifest using the evidence-signing service (HSM-backed KMS integration).
- Storage & delivery: upload artifact to tenant-scoped secure bucket with presigned-download link; record audit-export event in audit-log index.

Trade-offs and alternatives considered:
- Doing full join in the streaming layer vs. materializing normalized events into a persistent store and performing a batch join at export time. We choose streaming normalization plus short-term materialization (30 days) to balance cost and export latency.
- Signing with platform key vs. tenant-managed key. MVP will use platform HSM-backed key; roadmap includes tenant-supplied KMS integration.

Privacy and residency considerations:
- All artifacts will be created in the tenant's residency region to avoid cross-region transfer for residency-sensitive customers.
- Export manifest will include the exact location and retention TTL; automated retention enforcer will purge exported artifacts when TTL expires.

Operational metrics and SLOs:
- Export success rate >= 99.5% per week.
- Median export generation latency under 45s for windows <= 10k events.
- Alerting on sign failures, missing residency metadata, or incomplete correlation coverage (>5% unmatched RBAC assignments).

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Internal beta with engineering ops tenants: enable for two internal tenants, validate event coverage and signatures.
2) Closed beta with 3 enterprise customers who regularly request residency-aware evidence.
3) General availability with feature flag and per-tenant opt-in.

Risks and mitigations:
- Incomplete correlation (SAML logs missing): include best-effort notes in timeline and surface gaps in index.json so auditors are aware.
- Signing key compromise: rotate keys and provide revocation list; maintain previous manifests and revocation metadata for auditor continuity.
- Large export sizes for lengthy windows: provide split artifacts and streaming download option in follow-on work.

Dependencies:
- SCIM delta topic (ENG-12856 and related infra work) for reliable change stream.
- Evidence-signing service and KMS/HSM integration (security team deliverable).
- Tenant metadata API for residency/retention lookups.

Open questions (to resolve in discovery):
- Format preference for auditors (CSV vs. HTML narrative) — document both, default to CSV+HTML summary.
- Retention TTL for exported artifacts vs. tenant retention policy: default to min(tenant TTL, 90 days) unless customer requests longer retention.
- Whether to include raw SAML assertions in exports (privacy risk) — default to exclude raw assertions; include summarized session proof fields.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Spike (2d) to build a streaming normalizer prototype and generate a sample artifact for internal tenant. Owner: Tomás Rivera.
- Security review kickoff to scope signing and KMS controls. Owner: Aisha Patel.
- Draft PRD and compliance acceptance criteria for audit signoff. Owner: Product (Nikhil Rao).
